les: Toe die nuus met die pos gekom het

items.bewering: Seemanne het lank gelede by Tafelbaai briewe onder 'n gemerkte klip gelos.
items.bron: Franco Frescura, 'Colonial Post and Telegraph Diary of the Cape of Good Hope' (sahistory.org.za): the Table Bay stones from 1527 on, and the 1632 Dutch stone recording letters left beneath it. Also the Iziko/Maritime Museum audio-tour text (voicemap.me): from about 1615 European sailors left letters under the stones for ships sailing the other way. Frescura notes that not every stone marked letters; some only recorded a visit. The lesson's wording, a marked stone with letters under it, is accurate.

items.bewering: Die merke het die skip, sy kaptein en die datums gewys.
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): the 1632 stone names the commanders, the ships and the dates they arrived and left. Colvin, 'South Africa' (mainlesson.com): the custom of inscribing the ship's name, its captain and the dates of the visit. Hippon's 1607 inscription, 'ANT HIPON MA OF THE DRAGON 28 DECEMBER 1607', fits that pattern.

items.bewering: Die volgende skip se mense het geweet dat hulle daar moet kyk. Die seemanne kon net hoop dat daardie skip gou sou kom.
items.bron: Colvin (mainlesson.com): by 1591 the practice of leaving a packet of letters under an inscribed stone was well established, which is why later ships knew to look there. The voicemap/Maritime Museum text says the letters were left for whichever ship came by going the other way, with no schedule, so 'could only hope' fits. Frescura gives examples of letters damaged by waiting, such as the letter Middleton found buried and too wet to read.

items.bewering: Ons noem so 'n klip 'n posklip.
items.bron: The English name is well attested: 'post office stone(s)' (Frescura on sahistory.org.za; Colvin; Maritime Museum audio text). The practice itself is confirmed. Four searches in Afrikaans ('posklip', 'posklippe', 'posstene', 'poskantoorklippe') found no Afrikaans source using 'posklip' for these stones, from a museum, an archive or anywhere else. The word is a clear compound and may well be in use, but this is a claim about Afrikaans naming, and the check rule requires a South African source for it. A person should confirm that 'posklip' is the name used for the stones, or accept it as the lesson's own descriptive coinage. The same applies to the begrip entry 'posklip', whose definition is otherwise accurate.

items.bewering: 'n Gemerkte klip waaronder seemanne briewe vir 'n latere skip gelos het.
items.bron: Same sources as the stone claims above (Frescura diary, sahistory.org.za; Colvin; Maritime Museum audio text). The definition's content is accurate; the term itself is the open item above.

items.bewering: Aan die Kaap het ruiters te perd later die pos van dorp tot dorp geneem.
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): from 1807, horse posts ('Post Orderlies') replaced runners on the inland mails. Wikipedia, 'South African Post Office', and the search summary of the same history: in 1805 farmers on horseback carried postbags between Cape Town and Swellendam and Tulbagh. The claim is true. Note that the Khoikhoi runners on foot, who carried the post from 1803 to 1806, go unmentioned; that is an omission, not a falsehood.

items.bewering: 'n Brief se reis na 'n ver dorp het dae en soms selfs weke geduur.
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): Cape Town to Grahamstown mail ran only once a week until 1846, then twice a week, over roughly 900 km. Pony Express figures (nps.gov, legendsofamerica.com) put a relayed horse post at about 10 mph, or roughly 100 to 200 km a day with relays. At that pace the longer Cape routes took days, and a letter that missed a weekly post took more than a week. The wording is deliberately approximate and holds.

items.bewering: Al duisende jare gelede het mense in sommige lande posduiwe gebruik om boodskappe te dra.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post': probably as old as the ancient Persians, and used by the Romans more than 2000 years ago (Julius Caesar in Gaul). Popular claims of Egypt around 3000 BC are weakly sourced, but 'thousands of years' rests safely on the Roman evidence, and 'in sommige lande' is suitably narrow.

items.bewering: Duiwe, ruiters en skepe het in dieselfde tydperk pos gedra.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post': the siege of Paris in 1870-71 and the Great Barrier Island pigeongram service around 1897-1908. Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): horse posts at the Cape from 1807, and ships carrying mail to the UK through the 19th century. All three overlapped in the 1800s.

items.bewering: Mense het duiwe nog gebruik lank nadat daar poskantore en posseëls was.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post': the Paris siege pigeon post of 1870-71 carried about a million private messages, and France, Germany and Russia still kept large pigeon stocks when World War I began. Wikipedia, 'Postage stamps and postal history of the United Kingdom': the first stamp, the Penny Black, dates from 1840.

items.bewering: So 'n duif was vinniger as 'n ruiter.
items.bron: This is a comparative claim. Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post': Catalina Island pigeons flew 48 miles in about an hour, and racing pigeons average about 97 km/h over long distances (search summary). NPS, 'Pony Express' (nps.gov): a relayed horse post averaged about 10 mph. The pigeon was several times faster.

items.bewering: Maar 'n posduif vlieg net een kant toe, terug na sy eie hok. Mense moes 'n duif eers ver van sy hok af wegneem. Hulle het 'n klein briefie aan sy poot vasgemaak.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post': birds are carried in cages to a distant place, the messages are attached, and the pigeon flies back to its home. For the Great Barrier service, messages were tied to the legs, up to five per bird. That service ran one way, because the return route was not worth running. Paris's two-way traffic used two separate sets of birds: pigeons were taken out by balloon and then flew home. Each bird still flew one way. The claim holds.

items.bewering: Duiwepos kon daarom nooit 'n hele posstelsel wees nie.
items.bron: This is an absolute claim. Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post': every pigeon service, including the Great Barrier pigeongram companies that issued their own stamps, linked fixed points, because a bird can only fly to its own loft. None could carry a letter to any address, which is what the lesson's 'posstelsel' means (its begrip: deliveries to their addresses). Read against that definition the claim holds. Watch for any later rewording that calls pigeon post 'never a postal service' in general, because the Great Barrier services were commercial postal services within their limits.

items.bewering: 'n Duif wat 'n boodskap huis toe na sy eie hok dra.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pigeon post' (homing to its own loft). Accurate and consistent with the study block.

items.bewering: Mettertyd het dorpe poskantore gekry waar jy 'n brief kon inhandig. Jy het nie meer self iemand nodig gehad wat daardie kant toe reis nie.
items.bron: Search summary of the Cape postal history (Wikipedia, 'South African Post Office'; Frescura): before the reforms, private letter-writers depended on the goodwill of visitors, servants or pedlars; by 1852 there were 73 country post offices at the Cape.

items.bewering: Voorheen het die ontvanger meestal betaal, en die prys het van die afstand afgehang.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Postage stamps and postal history of the United Kingdom', and the Postal Museum, 'Rowland Hill's postal reforms': before 1840 the charge depended on distance and the number of sheets, and was usually collected from the recipient. 'Meestal' is suitably hedged.

items.bewering: Nuwe reëls het die pos toe baie goedkoper gemaak. Die stuurder het self vooruit betaal, volgens die brief se gewig. Binne een land het 'n brief dieselfde gekos, naby of ver.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Postage stamps and postal history of the United Kingdom': from 10 January 1840 the Uniform Penny Post charged 1d per half ounce whatever the distance, priced by weight, with prepayment by the sender (1d prepaid against 2d if unpaid). At the Cape, the Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za) records rates standardised at 4d per half ounce in 1846. One nuance does not make the claim false: prepayment was not compulsory at first, it was only made much cheaper.

items.bewering: Die posseël was die maklike manier om vooruit te betaal.
items.bron: Postal Museum, 'Rowland Hill's postal reforms': prepayment by stamped paper, envelopes and labels; the Penny Black, 6 May 1840. Frescura diary: the first Cape triangular stamps, 1 September 1853.

items.bewering: 'n Papiertjie wat jy op 'n brief plak om vooruit vir sy reis te betaal.
items.bron: Postal Museum, 'Rowland Hill's postal reforms' (stamps as labels showing prepayment). An accurate simple definition.

items.bewering: In die strate het posbusse verskyn waar briewe gewag het vir die posman.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Pillar box', and the States of Jersey report 'Historic Post Boxes in Jersey' (gov.je): the first roadside pillar boxes in St Helier in 1852, at Trollope's suggestion; the mainland followed in 1853-54. This came after stamps (1840), matching the lesson's order.

items.bewering: 'n Houer waarin briewe wag totdat hulle weggaan of afgehaal word.
items.bron: This covers both the street box (Wikipedia, 'Pillar box') and the private box from which mail is collected. The Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za) records that 'Private Boxes, later known as Post Boxes' were introduced at the Cape Town Post Office in January 1854. An accurate definition.

items.bewering: Treine het later sakke vol pos tussen stede vervoer.
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): the first Railway Travelling Post Office, the Western TPO, in 1882, in carriages fitted out as sorting offices. Search summary of the SA postal history: a dedicated mail train with special coaches in 1883.

items.bewering: Vragmotors het die pos tot by klein dorpies gebring.
items.bron: Search summary of the SA postal history (Wikipedia, 'South African Post Office'; ancestry24.co.za): motor transport introduced for the post in the 1900s, the first motor vehicle in 1911. Road motor mail to rural towns followed. This is a general claim and holds.

items.bewering: Vliegtuie het briewe oor die see na ver lande geneem.
items.bron: SAHistory, 'First airmail in SA' (sahistory.org.za): the 1911 Kenilworth-Muizenberg flight. Search summary: the first overseas airmail service from South Africa in 1932, and the Springbok service to Britain from 1945.

items.bewering: Elke nuwe masjien het die pos vinniger of verder laat kom.
items.bron: Follows from the sources above: horse post at about 10 mph, then rail, road and air. 'Vinniger of verder' is suitably loose.

items.bewering: Lank gelede was daar nog geen radio, televisie of internet in huise nie. Mense het dikwels eers van 'n groot gebeurtenis gehoor wanneer die pos aankom.
items.blok: Hoe die nuus by mense uitgekom het
items.bron: The postal histories above (Frescura; Wikipedia) show that letters and papers came by post in the 1800s, before broadcasting, which began in the 20th century. The telegraph existed from the mid-1800s but did not reach homes, so 'dikwels' is a fair hedge.

items.bewering: Koerante is met die pos na dorpe ver van die drukkerye af gestuur. In daardie koerante het mense van 'n nuwe wet of 'n komende verkiesing gelees.
items.blok: Hoe die nuus by mense uitgekom het
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): Cape inland newspaper postage rates (1857: colony-printed publications at 1d per ounce; 1882: the inland newspaper rate cut from 1d to ½d). Royal Mail Archive (aim25.com): the 1825 act allowing newspapers free transmission by post. That newspapers carried laws and elections is ordinary and uncontroversial.

items.bewering: 'n Brief van 'n ma het vertel wat by die huis gebeur. So het die pos families verbind wat ver van mekaar gewoon het.
items.blok: Hoe die nuus by mense uitgekom het
items.bron: This is an illustrative general statement. The History of Information page on the Penny Post (historyofinformation.com) calls the penny post a great stimulus to personal written communication.

items.bewering: Die posstelsel bestaan vandag nog, en die stappe het dieselfde gebly.
items.bron: SAPO Annual Report 2026 (pmg.org.za) and EWN, June 2026: the SA Post Office is still operating, with 657 branches. It has been in business rescue since July 2023, and an exit application is pending. 'Die stappe' (post, carry, deliver to an address) is a general, defensible characterisation. Because the claim is about SAPO's present state, it should be re-checked at any reprint, given the business rescue.

items.bewering: Party mense kry hul pos by die deur en ander by die poskantoor.
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): post boxes at the Cape Town Post Office since 1854. SAPO Annual Report 2026: street delivery and a branch network. Both modes are current South African practice.

items.bewering: Vandag dra 'n vragmotor of 'n vliegtuig die pos in plaas van 'n perd.
items.bron: Consistent with the motor and airmail history cited above (sahistory.org.za; Wikipedia, 'South African Post Office'), and with the Cape horse posts from 1807 (Frescura).

items.bewering: 'n Land se diens wat briewe en pakkies na hul adresse dra.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'South African Post Office': the national postal service, delivering letters and parcels, whose parcel licence was reapplied for in 2026 (businessreport.co.za). An accurate simple definition.

items.bewering: Die plek waar jy 'n brief inhandig en jou pos afhaal.
items.bron: Frescura diary (sahistory.org.za): post boxes at the post office from 1854, and the counter posting of letters. SAPO Annual Report 2026: the branch network. Accurate.

opsomming: Every factual claim held, including the two absolute or comparative claims about pigeon post ('vinniger as 'n ruiter' and 'nooit 'n hele posstelsel'), and the lesson has no analogies. One item needs a person: no Afrikaans source could be found that calls the Table Bay 'post office stones' 'posklip', so someone must confirm that name, or accept it, in the study block and its begrip entry before sign-off.
